answer: An agent network assigns voting power in proportion to tokens locked for a full voting epoch. A thousand accounts that mirror one owner's holdings get exactly the same combined weight as one account holding that balance, so a hollow swarm gains nothing from extra names. The accounting is crystal clear: to control 30 percent of the vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize 30 percent of all staked tokens, bearing the purchase cost and losing access to that capital until the epoch ends.
